description:
FILED s473a (Opus, 2026-09-07) while shipping #1243 (a).  The UNSUBSCRIPTED
spelling is fixed (`local($x) = @_` is now a list assignment); the
SUBSCRIPTED one is not, and this task carries the measurement that stopped it.

PROBE (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL at HEAD, scratch/s473a/probes/m1c.pl + m1d.pl):

  our @a = (9,9,9);  sub e { local($a[1]) = (7,8); return "in=$a[1]" }
    perl  in=7        PCL  in=8            <- scalar assignment: the comma op
  our $ar = [1,2,3]; sub e { local($ar->[1]) = (8,9); return "in=$ar->[1]" }
    perl  in=8        PCL  in=9
  our %h = (k=>"K");  sub e { local($h{k}) = ("P","Q"); return "in=$h{k}" }
    perl  in=P        PCL  in=Q

The RHS also runs in the WRONG CONTEXT, which is the wider half: `local($h{k})
= @list` stores the COUNT where perl stores $list[0], and a context-sensitive
call on the RHS is called in scalar context.

WHERE IT IS.  Pl::Parser::_process_local_declaration has an early
single-element path (Symbol + Subscript) reached through a pre-unwrap that
SPLICES the parens out of @non_ws, so the paren fact is gone by the time the
branch runs.  The unsubscripted spelling is fixed from $paren_lhs, recorded off
@$parts (which the unwrap does not touch).

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED WITH ITS TWIN â MEASURED, not guessed.  The fix was
written and reverted.  Routing a parenthesised single element to the existing
slice/list branch works (all shapes above become identical to perl; corpus-diff
showed local.t as the only mover, and its sweep counts were unchanged at
300/13, min_local.t 10/10, array.t 171/15, args.t 22/1), but it COSTS the
`p-local-*-elem-init` fast path, and that path is the one every
`local($SIG{__WARN__}) = sub {â¦}` / `local($ENV{K}) = â¦` / `local($h{k}) = $v`
site takes.  Interleaved min-of-7, same saved core, 3e6-iteration
`local($h{k}) = $_[0]` loop (scratch/s473a/probes/bench-*.lisp):

    p-local-hash-elem-init  -- today                          0.93 s
    p-local-hash-elem + (p-setf (p-hslice â¦) tmp)  -- the slice branch   1.14 s
    p-local-hash-elem + (p-list-= (vector PLACE) â¦)                1.27 s

So the general routing is a ~22 % pessimization of a common shape for a
divergence the whole perl-tests corpus does not contain (measured: emission
IDENTICAL over 111 files once the element half was reverted).  USER rule: flag
a bugfix that slows execution.

WHAT A FIX WOULD NEED: keep the `-init` macro when the RHS is scalar-shaped
(then list and scalar context coincide and the emission is unchanged) and take
the list path only when it is not.  That needs a licence on the RHS @rhs_parts
BEFORE it is parsed -- `_parse_expression` must be called exactly ONCE per
statement, so "parse it both ways and compare" is not available.  Either a
syntactic classifier over the parts (no top-level comma, no @/% term, no call)
or a cheap runtime primitive that takes element 0 of a list value without
building a slice.  Neither exists today; both are new mechanism, which is why
this is a task and not a branch.

BAR when taken: the three probe rows above plus `local($a[2]) = $a[2]` (the
stale-read case the -init macro exists for), `local(@a[0,1]) = (â¦)`, the
statement-modifier spellings, an unchanged emission for every scalar-RHS site
in perl-tests/local.t, and the benchmark above back at ~0.93 s.  Guard rows go
in Pl/t/local-list-assign-01.t, whose header already names this task as the
deliberate hole.
subject: SILENT WRONG: `local($a[1]) = (7,8)` (a PARENTHESISED subscripted target) is still a SCALAR assignment -- stores 8 where perl stores 7, and runs the RHS in scalar context; the general fix costs the p-local-*-elem-init fast path (measured 0.93 s -> 1.14 s)
